question: Why do 39 of the 3,708 residue genes carry an inhibitor of fitted strength above 1 -- the one reason `saturate.fit` refuses them at M2h's scale -- and what does that imply about the COMPILED LAYER rather than about those 39 genes? Is it a rule stating a removal response that large, a sign or unit convention read the wrong way round, or the bound s <= 1 cutting through the body of a continuous distribution of inhibitor folds?

questions.Q1_re_derivation: Q1. RE-DERIVATION. Running `lane-residuemult`'s own code path again from the 24 pinned compiled programs -- `compile.gate_program` at `combine2.SELECTION`, `combine2.multi_rule_genes`, `combine2.gene_rules`, `combine2.classify`, the mean fit before and after `scalefit.scaled_rho`, then `saturate.fit` on both -- how many residue genes are informative under NEITHER form, and how many of those are refused for `inhibitor_strength_above_1`? The count is taken from THIS run; `residuemult_lookup.json`'s committed per-gene table is then read on the `symbol` column alone and RECONCILED against it, set against set. A disagreement is a finding of this lane and is reported, never repaired.
questions.Q2_strength_distribution: Q2. THE DISTRIBUTION OF INHIBITOR STRENGTH among the 39. For each gene, the MAXIMUM over its inhibiting elements of IMPLIED_STRENGTH at the scale (the quantity that refused it), the same maximum unscaled, and the maximum raw removal fold RHO. Reported at QUANTILES with min, max and mean for each, over the 39 and never as a median alone. Also the SAME three distributions over every inhibiting element of the 39, not only each gene's worst, so that one gene with many inhibitors cannot stand for the set.
questions.Q3_how_many_inhibitors: Q3. HOW MANY INHIBITORS EACH OF THE 39 CARRIES: the distribution of `n_inhibiting` (elements with RHO > 1) and of `n_rules` over the 39, at QUANTILES with min and max, and the same two distributions over the whole residue and over every eligible multi-element gene, so that the 39's counts can be read against the population's instead of in isolation.
questions.Q4_one_inhibitor_or_several: Q4. ONE INHIBITOR OR SEVERAL. For each of the 39, how many of its inhibiting elements are themselves above the bound at the scale (IMPLIED_STRENGTH > 1 + STRENGTH_TOLERANCE). The distribution of that count, how many genes have exactly one offender, and -- for the genes with exactly one -- the share of the gene's inhibiting elements that the offender is. A single offending element on a gene with many inhibitors is a different object from a gene whose inhibitors are all that large, and the census must not merge them.
questions.Q5_where_the_rules_came_from: Q5. WHERE THE OFFENDING RULES CAME FROM. For every offending element of the 39, the compiled rule's evidence KIND (`bridge._kind`: predicted / experimental / curated / inferred / none), the evidence SOURCE string as the program states it, the `how` string `bridge.observation_of` returns (which says whether RHO was read from an evidence note's log2 fold change, from the rule strength below the clip, or from a CRISPRi EffectSize), the compiled cell label, and the chromosome. Reported as counts per category, plus the same counts over all inhibiting elements of all eligible genes as the background to read them against.
questions.Q6_outside_the_39: Q6. HOW MANY GENES OUTSIDE THE 39 CARRY AN INHIBITOR ABOVE 1. The question that decides whether the 39 are special at all, asked at both thresholds and over three nested populations: (a) the 3,708 residue; (b) the 12,500 the mean form excludes; (c) every eligible multi-element gene. In each, how many genes carry at least one inhibiting element with IMPLIED_STRENGTH above the bound AT THE SCALE, and how many unscaled, with the 39 removed from each count. If many genes outside the 39 carry one, then the 39 are not a distinguished set and this refusal is a general property of the compiled layer -- which would be the more important answer and is why this question is in the record before the count.
questions.Q7_threshold_or_tail: Q7. IS THE THRESHOLD AT A GAP OR IN THE BODY? Over every inhibiting element of every eligible gene, the distribution of IMPLIED_STRENGTH at the scale and unscaled at QUANTILES, and the NEAR-BAND counts: how many elements sit just below the bound (strength in [1/NEAR_BAND, 1]) and how many above it. If the just-below count is at least the above count, the bound cuts through the body of a continuous distribution and the threshold is doing the work; if the offenders are separated from it, they are a tail. BRANCHES fixes that wording before the counts are known.

implied_strength_definition: IMPLIED_STRENGTH(RHO) = (1 - 1/RHO) / H, `saturate.fit`'s own expression for an inhibitor's strength, with H = bridge.H_INTACT = 0.5 taken from the bridge and not re-declared. It is defined only for an inhibitor (RHO > 1), where it is the strength that makes that element alone, at intact occupancy, account for the whole observed fold. `combine2.fit`'s mean-form inhibitor strength is a DIFFERENT expression -- (RHO - 1) / (H * (q + RHO - 1)), which also depends on the gene's activators -- and it is reported beside this one for the 39 but it is not the quantity they were refused on.

implication_rule: THE BRANCH IS DECIDED BY THE NEAR-BAND COUNTS ALONE, over every inhibiting element of every eligible multi-element gene: `threshold_is_doing_the_work` when the number of elements with IMPLIED_STRENGTH in [1/NEAR_BAND, 1] at the scale is at least the number above 1 + STRENGTH_TOLERANCE, and `a_separated_tail` otherwise. NEAR_BAND = 1.2 and the comparison are both fixed here, before the count. The number of genes outside the 39 is reported in either wording and does not choose it.
implication: A SEPARATED TAIL: the offending folds are not continuous with the bound -- 69 inhibiting elements sit within a factor of 1.2 just below it against 192 above it -- so the 39 are refused on observations that stand apart from the population's inhibitor folds rather than on where a bound was drawn. 1160 eligible genes outside the 39 carry an inhibitor above the bound unscaled.
bound_checks: Checks whose violation is reported and never repaired. (a) MONOTONICITY: scaling moves an inhibitor's fold towards 1, so IMPLIED_STRENGTH at the scale is at most IMPLIED_STRENGTH unscaled for every inhibiting element -- a violation would mean `scalefit.scaled_rho` does not do what its docstring says. (b) THE REFUSAL IS THE OFFENDER: every gene this lane finds refused by `saturate.fit` at the scale for `inhibitor_strength_above_1` has at least one inhibiting element with IMPLIED_STRENGTH above 1 + STRENGTH_TOLERANCE, and every gene with such an element is refused -- the census quantity and the code's own refusal must agree gene for gene, or the census is measuring something else. (c) THE DERIVED THRESHOLDS: every offending element unscaled has RHO > 2 and every offending element at the scale has RHO > 1 + 1/SCALE, the two bounds `derived_thresholds` states by algebra. (d) SUBSET: the genes refused at the scale are a subset of those refused unscaled. (e) SIGN: every inhibiting element's compiled action is `inhibits`, which `combine2.classify` already enforces, re-asserted here so that a sign convention cannot pass unnoticed.
what_this_is_not: Not a test, not a registration, not a fit and not a claim about expression. No RNA value is opened. THIS LANE PROPOSES NO CHANGE TO ANY FIT, no new form, no new threshold and no repair: it states what the compiled layer's inhibitor folds are and where the existing bound falls among them, and stops there. `lane-multrna`'s outcome on measured RNA was WORSE and is carried forward unchanged: the multiplicative form being the one that CAN RUN these genes is not the multiplicative form reading closer to measured RNA on them.
limitations: A CENSUS of the compiled layer's own numbers. Every value is arithmetic on stated removal responses; nothing here is evidence that any of those responses is correct.

The compiled rules are overwhelmingly PREDICTED (`lane-residuemult` recorded 43,681 predicted against 19 experimental rules gated on chr1 alone). A census of predicted folds says what the predictor asserts, not what a cell does.
IMPLIED_STRENGTH assumes the bridge's intact occupancy H = 0.5 and the single-mechanism mapping. The strength of an inhibitor is not observable; it is this mapping's image of an observed fold.
The 39 are a predictor-side refusal count. Whether those genes' RNA is well or badly predicted is not asked and cannot be read off anything here.
Q6's populations are nested and the counts are of GENES, not elements; a gene with several offending elements counts once. Both are reported so neither can be mistaken for the other.
The NEAR_BAND of 1.2 is a choice, fixed before the count. A different band would move the just-below count; the quantiles of the full distribution are reported so the band cannot hide the shape.
Nothing in this lane distinguishes a correct large fold from a sign or unit error upstream. It can only say which rules the large folds come from, by evidence kind and `how` string.
The scale is M2h's multiplicative-form scale, taken as a constant and not re-estimated; M2h's own heterogeneity finding (`40b0a8d`: not consistent with a single global scale) applies to it here too.

money: none: no request is sent and no key is read

sources.accession: the 24 compiled non-coding programs 7d, 7h, lane-residue and lane-residuemult ran
reader v1 ENCODE DNase-seq narrowPeak files, 13 biosamples

exclusions: 7d's own: one rule, rules in several programs, a measured rule, an unreadable or exactly-1 observation, an action that disagrees with it, no activating rule
an element with RHO < 1 is an activator and is not in any inhibitor distribution here
a gene with no inhibiting element contributes to the gene counts and to no strength distribution
result_manifest.partitions: n/a: a predictor-side census; no outcome read and no RNA opened

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record 6511cfe

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
